content.comment_body: I'm updating my program; I've made changes on my PC and can successfully download it to the [product_name] without issues. Now, I need to transfer the updated program onto my memory card. I'm using [product_name] software [version_no]. The controller is [article_no] and the memory card is [article_no]. The card has an existing program and can load it into the controller at startup, or download from card to controller. However, when trying to transfer from controller to card, I get a confirmation prompt. Upon confirming, an 'ERROR' appears and I'm instructed to press ESC. Any suggestions for what I'm doing incorrectly?
What color is your memory card? Is it capable of both reading and writing, or is it read-only? Refer to this link for more information: [url]

To answer your question, my cards are light brown/yellow. Based on recent tests, I found that with an older [product_name] controller ([article_no]), I can read and write to these cards. I can transfer the program from this card to a newer controller ([article_no]), where it runs from the card. Transferring from card to controller seems possible, but if I remove the card, the program isn’t retained in the controller’s memory. I’ve tried this with two different newer controllers and observed the same results.

Your light brown module can be written to using [product_name] controllers with older [version_no], but the newer [version_no] controller can only read from it. To write to a card with the newer controller, use the violet or dark brown card with a backup battery. See the data sheet here: [url]. The memory card replaces the internal memory only during operation—if you unplug it, the program remains on the card, not in the controller. For copy protection, set a password in your project; then the card can only be used or erased by a controller with a display if the password is unknown. Hope this helps. Best regards, [user_name]

Thank you, [user_name]. I ordered [article_no] last Friday from RS, expecting delivery tomorrow. I’ll try it out and report the results. Based on the information from your link, that number matches the violet memory card, so hopefully this resolves my issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced challenges transferring programs between the controller and memory cards due to hardware version differences and specific card compatibility. Writing to light brown/yellow cards worked with older controllers but caused errors with newer hardware. The unclear error messages and lack of guidance about compatibility led to confusion regarding card capabilities and program retention.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy and consistent way to save or write controller programs to memory cards, regardless of controller version. They want clear feedback on compatibility issues or procedural limits so they can avoid errors and know when a specific card type is required.
